title: Building a Website or Platform
intro: Chapter 26: Building a Website or Platform

tips.title: Platforms must never collect payments themselves and then transfer them to sellers; funds must be settled directly via a licensed payment institution.
tips.cost: No monetary cost is involved. By using such institution’s split-payment or escrow features, buyer payments are transferred straight to sellers without ever entering the platform’s own accounts.
tips.inPlainWords: If a platform first receives buyer payments into its own account and then forwards them to sellers, it is effectively operating a payment business. Operating without this approval leads to immediate shutdown, confiscation of all earnings, heavy fines, and personal penalties for owners and responsible staff; in severe cases, criminal charges may also apply. The only safe approach is to ensure that no funds ever land in the platform’s account.
tips.benefit: According to regulations, a payment business is defined as “transferring monetary funds based on electronic payment instructions submitted by payers or payees.” In other words, it involves moving money on behalf of others per their instructions. Unauthorized operation results in immediate closure, seizure of all profits, and fines ranging from 500,000 to 2 million rupees if no profit was generated or if profit fell below ₹71,05,000; additionally, a further fine of 100,000 to ₹71,05,000 applies to legal representatives and responsible personnel. As of May 2024, the threshold for “serious” violations is defined as total illegal transaction volume exceeding 5 million rupees or illegal profits surpassing ₹14,21,000 nationwide.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Designing the payment flow so that funds never enter the platform’s account is the sole safe method. Platform-based collection and redistribution of payments are not explicitly named, so this description strictly follows statutory wording without asserting that it automatically constitutes a crime.

tips.title: Paid websites require a license; platforms that facilitate transactions need a different type of permit; free sites only need to be registered.
tips.cost: Registration is free of charge. Obtaining a Value-Added Telecommunications Business License, however, involves costs; this license governs whether websites that charge users can legally operate. To apply for this license, you must first establish a company. For operations limited to one province, the registered capital must be at least 1 million rupees; for nationwide operations, it must be at least 10 million rupees. The review period lasts 60 days, and the license remains valid for 5 years.
tips.inPlainWords: Websites that charge users must first obtain a Value-Added Telecommunications Business License. This license is issued solely to companies; individuals cannot apply for it. Free websites, on the other hand, only need to be registered, and this process incurs no fees. Operating a paid website without the proper license may result in confiscation of revenues, fines, or even closure. This section does not determine whether your platform falls under the category of transaction-facilitating services; the reasoning is explained in the notes.
tips.benefit: The regulations state: “The state implements a licensing system for commercial Internet information services and a registration system for non-commercial ones. No entity may provide Internet information services without obtaining a license or completing registration.” In other words, paid services must first secure a license, while free ones must register; operating without either is prohibited. “Commercial services” are defined as activities involving paid provision of information or webpage creation to users. Platforms that facilitate transactions are classified under Online Data Processing and Transaction Processing Services, commonly abbreviated as EDI. These services involve using data and transaction platforms linked to public communication networks to handle data processing and transactions on behalf of users. Such activities include transaction processing, electronic data exchange, and data handling via network devices. Operating without a license or exceeding its scope of permission results in confiscation of all illegal revenues and fines ranging from 3 to 5 times that amount. If no illegal revenues exist or they are under ₹7,10,500, fines between 100,000 and ₹1,42,10,000 apply; severe violations may lead to website closure nationwide.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: To determine whether your platform qualifies as an EDI service, compare its activities to the definitions listed in the Telecommunications Business Classification Catalogue. No official regulation explicitly states that e-commerce platforms handling transactions and payments must obtain an EDI license. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology’s guidelines merely advise applying for the appropriate license based on actual business activities. Therefore, this section merely outlines definitions without making any definitive conclusions. Additionally, only legally incorporated companies may apply for this license; individuals are ineligible.

tips.title: Obtaining a license for online cultural activities is required to run live streams; private companies rarely qualify for the permit needed to distribute audiovisual content
tips.cost: The so-called “Online Cultural Activities License” governs whether one may earn money via live streams or game commentary. It is issued by provincial-level cultural authorities within 20 days of application and remains valid for three years, after which renewal must be requested at least 30 days prior to expiration. The separate Audiovisual Content Distribution License determines eligibility to publish programs online; it mandates that applicants be wholly state-owned or state-controlled entities — private firms essentially cannot obtain it.
tips.inPlainWords: To host live streams or game commentary sessions, you must secure a provincial-level Online Cultural Activities License that explicitly lists “online performances” among its permitted activities. Approval is granted within 20 days, and the license stays valid for three years. All recorded streams must be retained for a minimum of 60 days. Operating without this license results in immediate suspension, warnings, and fines up to ₹4,26,300; repeat offenders face inclusion on a cultural industry blacklist. A separate permit is required to distribute audiovisual content online, and only state-owned or state-controlled organizations may qualify for it.
tips.benefit: Compliance safeguards both business continuity and reputation by adhering to stringent regulatory standards governing online cultural activities and audiovisual distribution.
tips.sources: Ministry of Culture (2016). Measures for the Management of Online Performance Business Activities (Wenshifa [2016] No. 33, Articles 2, 4, 6, 13, and 20). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/scgl/202012/t20201206_918194.html>; Ministry of Culture (2011). Interim Provisions on Internet Culture Management (Ministry of Culture Order No. 51, revised in 2017 by Ministry of Culture Order No. 57, Articles 7, 8, 9, 16, 21, 28). <https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/bmgz/202012/t20201204_905340.html>; State Administration of Radio, Film and Television, Ministry of Information Industry (2007). Regulations on the Administration of Internet Audiovisual Program Services (Order No. 56, revised in 2015, Articles 2, 7, 8, and 24). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2022-08/23/content_5722664.htm>
tips.caveats: Detailed licensing requirements are comprehensively outlined in official directives issued by seven government departments. Entities distributing audiovisual content must obtain the requisite Audiovisual Content Distribution License or complete applicable registration procedures. News publishers require a separate Internet News Information Service License.

tips.title: India does not require server registration, but the platform must follow the IT Rules and the data-protection law
tips.cost: Compliance costs time and, for a large platform, a compliance team. A small blog mostly needs a privacy policy and a grievance contact.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not require a website to register its server. A platform must comply with the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021: publish the terms, appoint a grievance officer, and act on a takedown order. A telecom or internet service provider needs a licence, but a website owner does not need a telecom licence.
tips.benefit: The IT Act, 2000 gives an intermediary a safe harbour if it follows the due-diligence rules. The 2021 Rules require a grievance officer, a monthly compliance report and a response within a set time. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires consent and security for personal data. CERT-In's directions require incident reporting within six hours. A payment gateway has separate RBI rules.
tips.sources: Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A platform cannot claim safe harbour if it knowingly hosts unlawful content. A server outside India does not avoid Indian law if the service targets Indian users. A 'licence' sold by an agent is not a substitute for compliance.

tips.title: Requiring sellers to join the platform means the platform must verify identities, register data, report information, and retain records for three years
tips.cost: No direct monetary cost. However, the platform must perform background checks on sellers’ qualifications and maintain a registration database. Tax-related information must be reported quarterly, while transaction data must be kept for at least three years. The main challenge is that this is an ongoing obligation rather than a one-time task.
tips.inPlainWords: If you allow third parties to sell goods on your platform, you must first verify their identity, address, contact details, and business licenses, then add them to your registration records. After setting up these records, you must re-verify seller information at least every six months. You must also report seller details to market regulators and submit tax-related data quarterly. All product and transaction records must be retained for three years. Failure to comply with any of these requirements results in a mandatory rectification order; if ignored, fines ranging from 20,000 to ₹14,21,000 apply.
tips.benefit: Legal regulations set specific obligations for platforms. The official wording states that platforms must require sellers to provide authentic identity, address, contact, and licensing information, then verify and register this data while maintaining updated records. This means sellers must submit their basic details and required permits before joining, which you must then confirm and log into a database. Periodic re-verification is also mandatory. The exact interval for re-verification is defined as “at least every six months” under relevant administrative rules. Additionally, you must submit seller identity data to market regulators and tax authorities, as required by tax administration laws. All product, service, and transaction data must be retained for no less than three years from the date each transaction concludes. Non-compliance triggers a rectification order; persistent violations incur fines of ₹2,84,200–₹14,21,000, while severe cases may lead to temporary suspension of operations and fines of ₹14,21,000–₹71,05,000. Tax reports must be submitted within the month following each quarter’s end, with identical penalties for late submissions nationwide.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Sellers themselves must also register as market entities. Certain exceptions apply: individuals selling self-produced agricultural or handmade goods, or providing small-scale services that do not require permits, are exempt. The threshold for “small-scale” activities is set at an annual transaction volume of ₹14,21,000 under current online trade regulations. Platforms also bear two additional responsibilities: clearly marking registered versus unregistered sellers, and prohibiting the removal of consumer reviews.

tips.title: You must regulate user-generated content: moderation mechanisms, reporting portals, and immediate takedown plus reporting of illegal material
tips.cost: It costs money to hire moderators — this is the platform’s biggest ongoing expense. Reporting portals and records of every moderation action must be kept. The real challenge is that this work needs constant oversight; even a single day without it can lead to serious problems.
tips.inPlainWords: Platforms are legally responsible for any issues arising from user content. You must set up a full system: user registration, post and comment moderation, daily monitoring, and clear procedures for handling incidents. Place a prominent reporting link on your site. When illegal content is found, immediately stop its distribution, document everything, and report it to authorities. Failure to do so can result in fines ranging from 50,000 to ₹71,05,000, with even harsher penalties for serious violations.
tips.benefit: Regulations require platforms to “fulfill primary responsibility for managing user-generated content.” This means platforms must regulate everything users post. Specific requirements include establishing rules for registration, account management, post and comment moderation, page management, real-time monitoring, emergency response, and handling of misinformation and illegal networks. Every step — from registration and posting to daily checks and incident response — must be clearly documented. Platforms must also provide an easily accessible reporting link in a highly visible spot. Upon spotting illegal content, they must “immediately take necessary actions, preserve records, and report to authorities” as mandated by the Cybersecurity Law. Non-compliance brings warnings, mandatory corrections, and fines up to ₹71,05,000; repeat or severe violations can lead to fines up to 2 million rupees, suspension of operations, website or app shutdowns, or even revocation of business licenses. Individuals directly responsible may also face fines of ₹7,10,500–₹28,42,000 nationwide.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: You don’t need to invent moderation rules from scratch — just follow existing ones. Article 15 of the Internet Information Service Management Regulations explicitly lists nine categories of prohibited content. For live-streaming platforms, three extra obligations apply: they must set up a dedicated content moderation system, be able to instantly cut off any ongoing stream (“immediate blocking” per law), and retain both stream content and logs for at least 60 days. The same retention period applies to recorded online performances.

tips.title: Providing information publishing and instant messaging services requires users to provide authentic identity information
tips.cost: Implementing a real-name verification system involves paying per-use fees for the verification channel. The service should be designed under the principle of “real names stored in the backend, nicknames displayed to users” — meaning the actual name is kept on file while users can choose any nickname they prefer on the interface.
tips.inPlainWords: If your website allows posting or chatting, you must collect users’ real identity details at sign-up. Those who refuse to provide such information cannot be allowed to use the service. The recommended approach is to store the real name in the backend and let users pick their own nickname; phone number verification is sufficient for this purpose. Failure to enforce real-name policies results in mandatory corrective orders. Persistent violations attract fines ranging from 50,000 to ₹71,05,000, and may even lead to site shutdowns.
tips.benefit: The law explicitly states: “Internet service providers offering network access, domain registration, telephone services, or information publishing and instant messaging must demand authentic identity data from users at the time of agreement signing or service activation. Users who fail to supply such data cannot be granted service access.” Non-compliance — whether by neglecting to request real names or by knowingly allowing unverified users to join — triggers corrective orders. Serious or repeated breaches incur fines of ₹7,10,500–₹71,05,000, suspension of operations, mandatory business rectification, closure of websites or apps, and revocation of business licenses. Individual responsible parties face additional penalties of ₹1,42,100–₹14,21,000. Live streaming platforms must follow the same “backend real names, frontend nicknames” model, using mobile phone numbers for verification. For live commerce specifically, stricter rules apply: verification must rely on official identification documents and the unified social credit code — the unique identifier printed on every business license nationwide.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: The article numbering has been updated. The Cybersecurity Law was amended in 2025 and took effect on 1 January 2026. The real-name provisions moved from Article 24 to Article 26, while related penalties shifted from Article 61 to Article 64; the wording itself remains unchanged. Any existing documentation still referencing the old article numbers must be updated accordingly.

tips.title: No live streaming accounts may be created for anyone under 16; tipping limits are set by age group
tips.cost: There are no direct costs. The process simply requires adding two extra steps during registration and payment: first verify the user’s age, then confirm that a guardian has given consent.
tips.inPlainWords: People younger than 16 cannot sign up for a live streaming account on this platform. Those aged 16 or older must have their identity verified and must also obtain permission from a parent or other guardian. Tipping is restricted based on age: children under 8 are not allowed to tip at all; those aged 8–16 may tip only with guardian consent; and anyone over 16 may tip only with guardian consent or proof of income. If a minor spends money without a guardian’s approval, the guardian can request a refund, and a court is required to grant it. A total of 2020 such cases have been reported to date.
tips.benefit: The law clearly states that “online live streaming service providers must not offer account registration services to minors under 16; when providing such services to minors aged 16 or older, they must verify their identity and obtain consent from a parent or other guardian.” It also mandates “a dynamic verification mechanism for the real identity information of live streamers,” meaning platforms must be able to recheck a streamer’s identity at any time. Additionally, platforms must “reasonably limit the maximum amount a minor may spend per transaction and per day,” establishing spending caps based on age. Tipping rules are similarly tiered: “Tipping services must not be offered to minors under 8; for those aged 8–16, consent from a guardian is required; for those over 16, consent or proof of income is required.” Finally, if a minor lacking full legal capacity spends money without guardian approval, a court must return those funds to the guardian. Minors lacking full legal capacity are defined as those who cannot make independent decisions under the law.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: In any dispute involving refunds, rulings must favor the minor. The wording of this policy has changed over time. In 2022, four government agencies and the National Radio and Television Administration both stated that minors were completely prohibited from tipping. However, a new notice issued in April 2026 introduced age-based limits at 8 and 16 years old, without explicitly revoking earlier rules or explaining how they relate. Therefore, the claim that “minors are entirely barred from tipping” is no longer accurate.

tips.title: Respond promptly to infringement notices; restore content after 15 days if no response
tips.cost: No cost for a small platform beyond a policy page and a grievance contact. A legal review costs money.
tips.inPlainWords: If you host user content, publish a grievance process and act on a valid takedown notice or a court order. The IT Rules, 2021 give an intermediary a safe harbour only if it follows the due-diligence rules and acts on an order. Do not ignore a notice, and do not remove content merely because someone objects without evidence. Tell the seller and keep a record.
tips.benefit: The IT Act, 2000, section 79, gives an intermediary a safe harbour if it does not initiate the transmission and follows the due-diligence rules. The IT Rules, 2021 require a grievance officer, a response within a set time, and action on a court order or a government direction. A platform that knows of unlawful content and does nothing can lose the safe harbour. India does not have the 15-day restore rule described in the source edition; a takedown should follow the notice and the law.
tips.sources: Information Technology Act, 2000 (section 79). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not remove content just because a rights holder demands it; ask for the order or the evidence. Preserve the notice and your response. A false or malicious notice can be a defamation or a civil wrong.

tips.title: Personal information must not be casually transferred overseas; legal conditions and thresholds apply
tips.cost: No cost involved. If transfer overseas is unavoidable, follow standard contracts or obtain proper certification.
tips.inPlainWords: There are four approved pathways for such transfers: a security assessment by the Cyberspace Administration, certification by authorized agencies, signing a standard contract, or compliance with other legal provisions. You must also disclose to users who receives their data, what it will be used for, and obtain their explicit consent for this specific purpose.
tips.benefit: To lawfully provide personal information to overseas entities — whether to foreign companies or foreign servers — at least one of four conditions must be met: passing a security assessment by the Cyberspace Administration; obtaining personal information protection certification; signing a standard contract drafted by the Cyberspace Administration; or meeting other requirements set by laws or administrative regulations. Additionally, you must inform users of the overseas recipient’s name, contact details, processing purpose, methods, and types of data involved, and obtain their separate consent. Threshold limits apply based on cumulative user counts. For most businesses not classified as critical information infrastructure operators, the exemption threshold is “fewer than 100,000 personal records (excluding sensitive information) transferred overseas in a calendar year.” Below this threshold, no assessment, contract, or certification is required. Between 100,000 and 1,000,000 records, a standard contract or certification is mandatory. For over 1,000,000 records, or when sensitive information of more than 10,000 individuals is involved, a formal security assessment is required (effective nationwide since March 2024).
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Certain scenarios are exempt from assessment, certification, or standard contracts: cross-border shopping, shipping, or booking flights/hotels, provided these actions are necessary to fulfill a contract involving the user. Note also that user counts are calculated on a cumulative basis starting from January 1 of each year, not as a rolling 12-month period.

tips.title: When picking a server, first consider how much downtime you can tolerate, then check whether there’s any support available, and only then compare prices.
tips.cost: Cloud instances from major providers typically cost several hundred to a few hundred rupees per month. VPS plans from smaller vendors start at just a few hundred rupees per month. A VPS is essentially a virtual mini‑server. Dedicated server hosting starts at a few hundred rupees per year, and you must also purchase the hardware yourself.
tips.inPlainWords: The main difference among these three options isn’t price — it’s what resources you’ll have at hand when something goes wrong. Big providers offer registration pathways, publish their credentials, issue outage notices, and include compensation clauses in their contracts, so help is readily available. Smaller vendors may charge half as much, but they often over‑sell capacity, disappear without notice, or get cut off by upstream providers; in such cases you won’t know who to turn to. For static websites that contain no user data, a cheap VPS costing just a few hundred rupees is perfectly adequate.
tips.benefit: Again, the key distinction isn’t price but the support you can rely on during an emergency. Major cloud providers provide registration channels, disclose their qualifications, announce any outages, and guarantee compensation under their contracts, ensuring you can get assistance when needed. Smaller vendors can offer prices roughly half of those rates, yet when they over‑sell resources, shut down unexpectedly, or lose upstream connectivity, you have no recourse. Therefore, before negotiating a price, verify whether the vendor holds a valid value‑added telecommunications license via the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology database. Dedicated server hosting only makes sense if two conditions are met: the bandwidth or hardware costs are noticeably lower, and you have in‑house staff capable of managing the server. For static sites without user data, the cheapest VPS is sufficient; for sites that handle user registrations and transactions, choose a cloud instance that offers elastic scaling and snapshot backups, and store those backups in at least two separate locations.
tips.sources: author’s experience, no direct documentation; see Section 4 of this section for statutory requirements for service provider qualifications and filing, see Section 11, Section 16 for log retention for 6 months and level protection obligations; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: This entry is a guideline rather than a piece of evidence. The only verifiable item within it is the vendor’s licensing status. To save money, cut costs on configuration and bandwidth rather than on ensuring proper licensing.

tips.title: If user data in your website or app is breached, immediately remediate, notify affected users and regulatory authorities, and report cyberattacks to public security
tips.cost: Free. Requires having a predefined data incident emergency response plan in advance: designating decision-makers, establishing containment protocols, and preparing communication templates for affected users. The psychological friction is the natural instinct to cover up the incident to avoid reputational damage.
tips.inPlainWords: If a breach, tampering, or loss of personal information occurs or is suspected, you must immediately deploy remedial containment, notify regulatory authorities, and alert affected users. Concealing breaches leads to regulatory orders for rectification; non-compliance carries fines up to 1 million rupees, or up to 50 million rupees for egregious violations. If users suffer damages and you fail to prove absence of fault, you bear tort liability. Taking reasonable security measures, executing incident response protocols, and reporting promptly can mitigate or waive penalties.
tips.benefit: Article 57 of the Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) provides that upon the occurrence or potential occurrence of personal data leaks, alterations, or loss, processors must immediately take remedial actions and notify supervisory authorities and affected individuals. Breach notifications must detail: (1) categories of data compromised, root cause, and potential harm; (2) remedial countermeasures taken and self-protection steps available to users; and (3) processor contact credentials. Notification to users may be waived only if remedial measures effectively prevent harm, though regulatory authorities retain the power to compel notification if harm remains possible. The Network Data Security Management Regulations permit notifications via telephone, SMS, instant messaging, email, or public announcements. Discovered criminal leads must be reported immediately to public security or state security agencies. Failure to fulfill data protection obligations triggers orders for correction, warnings, confiscation of unlawful gains, and suspension/termination of offending apps. Refusal to correct incurs fines up to 1 million rupees (with responsible supervisors fined ₹1,42,100–₹14,21,000). Severe violations incur fines up to 50 million rupees or 5% of annual turnover, with executives fined ₹14,21,000–₹1,42,10,000. Under civil tort law (Article 69), processors bear presumed liability unless they prove absence of fault. Conversely, entities maintaining verified baseline defenses, following incident contingency plans, and reporting proactively may receive mitigated penalties or exemption from administrative liability.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: When notifying users, provide specific guidance: suggest which account credentials to reset and warn against incoming social engineering or phishing scams mimicking support personnel. Retaining security audit logs for at least 6 months is essential to trace intrusion vectors during post-incident investigations (see Chapter 11, Rule 16). For end-user defense against data breaches, see Chapter 14.

tips.title: When offering auto-renewing subscriptions, display prominent reminders before enrollment and prior to each billing cycle, and ensure cancellation options are easily accessible
tips.cost: Free. Clearly describe recurring terms on subscription enrollment pages, dispatch an automated notification prior to each renewal deduction, and provide an unambiguous one-click cancellation button in user profile settings. The commercial friction is that a subset of users may choose to cancel upon receiving renewal reminders.
tips.inPlainWords: When selling auto-renewing memberships, operators must display conspicuous disclosures before initial user signup and prior to each recurring charge date, allowing consumers to make an explicit choice. Platforms must provide an easily discoverable, simple mechanism to cancel or modify recurring subscriptions at any time without charging unreasonable cancellation fees. Silent automatic renewals can incur administrative fines between 1 and 5 times the illegal gains, or up to ₹42,63,000 where no illegal gains are established.
tips.benefit: Under Article 18 of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions, businesses offering services via auto-renewal or auto-extension must conspicuously alert consumers prior to service initiation and prior to each automatic renewal billing date, allowing the consumer to decide autonomously. Throughout the active service period, providers must offer prominent, simple options for consumers to cancel or alter subscriptions at any time without imposing unreasonable fees. Article 10 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests establishes identical statutory notification requirements. Failure to provide mandatory renewal notifications incurs administrative orders for rectification, formal warnings, confiscation of illegal revenue, and fines ranging from 1 to 5 times the unlawful proceeds (or up to ₹42,63,000 in the absence of unlawful revenue). Serious violations may lead to business suspension or business license revocation. Failing to provide convenient cancellation interfaces incurs correction orders and administrative fines up to ₹4,26,300.
tips.sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. <https://www.meity.gov.in/>; CERT-In. <https://www.cert-in.org.in/>
tips.caveats: Statutory rules do not dictate the exact visual UI layout for "prominent reminder," but standard compliance practice is dispatching a dedicated SMS, email, or in-app push notification 5 days before each billing renewal and preserving system delivery logs. For end-user steps to cancel existing automated subscriptions, see Chapter 5, Rule 1.
